title: The planning exam hp_gate_v2: six checks judged by code, pinned, run once on fresh held-out tables and people
request: The owner chose the planning gate (G1) as the next gap: hp_gate_v1 could not be run. Keep check 3 (people); 300 seconds and EUR 0.03 a project; held-out tables and people written by another session.
spec: Every check judged by code; terms and held-out digests pinned before the run; projects built on the product's own unattended path; the rules arm with no model; rows stay in agent_runs and only counts are committed; run once.
plan: write gate.py with the six checks and the pin
write run.py: one case built by one arm on the product path
two adversarial reviews before the pin
pin, run the tables, run the people, judge once

decisions.decision: Count a catch asked on the project page as obeyed
decisions.why: the unattended build goes on with an open question by design (stage H5); v1 counted only a stopped build

decisions.decision: Check 5 decides which plan serves; it does not fail the gate
decisions.why: a model plan that is not better should simply not serve

decisions.decision: The tables run is sealed: shape in the log, whole calls with thinking in the exam vault
decisions.why: held-out briefs and column names must never reach a training set

decisions.decision: Nobody changing planning reads a row of the run
decisions.why: reading the rows would spend the held-out set for any later claim

change: dclab_rnd/agent_eval/planning_gate_v2/{__init__,gate,run}.py, gate_v2.sha256, held/ (written by another session), tests/test_planning_gate_v2.py; result evidence/campaigns/planning_gate_v2/.

findings.defect: A spent cap or a dead key turned the model arm into the rules arm without stopping the run.
findings.scenario: --cap-eur 0.5 crossed at case 5: cases 5 to 8 ran the rules plan as the model's and rows.json said stopped null.
findings.cause: plan_with_model catches every exception and plan_project keeps the rules plan.
findings.fix: Watched wraps the model view and records every failed request; the run stops on one.

findings.defect: Check 1 counted the plan's designed questions as disobeyed.
findings.scenario: A post-outcome catch the plan could not confirm was asked, the final stage ran, check 1 fell below 1.0 even with the rules serving.
findings.cause: obeyed read every enforceable catch that was not applied as a failure.
findings.fix: asked catches (matched by kind and column) and a split's own column count as obeyed.

findings.defect: Half of 'nothing lost' could never fail.
findings.scenario: The model arm applies the rules plan first and plans only add columns, so its forbidden set always held the rules'.
findings.cause: it compared forbidden sets, not what each plan caught.
findings.fix: compare the model plan's own forbid catches with the rules plan's on the same project.

findings.defect: The one allowed run could be wasted before any model call.
findings.scenario: A missing make_ function exited with no rows.json; tables then refused every rerun and judge crashed.
findings.cause: directory made before any check; rows written only on success.
findings.fix: preflight counts cases, traps and pairs first; rows.json written in finally.

findings.defect: Held-out column names and case ids could reach the committed result.
findings.scenario: Check 2 listed the columns put back; the stop message carried a pandas error text.
findings.fix: gate.public keeps counts, means and met only; the whole verdict stays in the run folder.

findings.defect: Check 1 passed with no trap read.
findings.scenario: 14 built projects with no catch plus one stopped case: met.
findings.fix: met is None unless a trap was read.

findings.defect: Check 6 averaged zeros it never measured.
findings.scenario: Stopped projects carried 0 s; the rules plan was never timed, so 'rules serve' always met check 6.
findings.fix: average only projects where a plan was made; the rules plan is timed in both arms.

findings.defect: Check 5 threw away the second seed.
findings.scenario: 8 cases on 2 seeds gave at most 8 pairs; one case with no planted trap would leave check 5 unread and fail the gate.

findings.defect: Check 4 counted the project id as a number nobody gave.
findings.scenario: 22% of random hex ids start with a digit; all 32 clean had probability 0.0003.
findings.cause: the report names the project by its id.
findings.fix: the id is removed from the report before the number check.

findings.defect: A model that never answered was hidden.
findings.scenario: No model configured: Watched wrapped None, the AttributeError fell back to the rules plan, model_errors stayed empty.
findings.cause: Watched did not check for a None client.
findings.fix: a None client and a failed client request are recorded as errors.

findings.defect: Stage notes called a live model outside the run's cap and folder, in both arms.
findings.scenario: explain_stage and llm_critique used the process's default gateway, kept held-out stage records in the workspace.
findings.cause: the run's gateway was never installed for the stages.
findings.fix: the build runs inside notes_off(); the rules' notes stand.

findings.defect: An interrupted run read as complete; a judge without people locked the gate as failed; an incomplete people run was accepted.
findings.scenario: Ctrl-C wrote rows.json with stopped null; judge with no --people wrote HPG-001.
findings.cause: the defaults were the happy path.
findings.fix: stopped starts as 'interrupted' with an 'of' count; judge needs --people and a complete run.

findings.defect: The planner enforces only about a third of the traps the case authors planted.
findings.scenario: Held-out tables, 16 pairs: 0.29 of planted traps enforced by the rules, 0.35 by the model.
findings.cause: not read: the rows stay unread by the gate's rule.
findings.fix: none yet: needs a dev set that reproduces it.

measurements.name: hp_gate_v2 on its held-out tables (8 cases x 2 seeds x 2 arms) and people (plan_held, 8)
measurements.result: failed: check 1 69/73 (0.945); check 2 one model plan dropped a rules catch; check 3 gaps +0.125 planning, +0.25 understanding, 1 blocked run; check 4 two projects failed with nothing built; check 5 rules 0.29 vs model 0.35, +0.06 [0.00, 0.16], the rules serve; check 6 met (0.019 s, EUR 0)
measurements.next: a dev set that reproduces the four failing counts, then fresh held-out material for hp_gate_v3
limits: people run conversations not sealed by the harness

outcome: The planning exam ran once and failed on four counts. The model's plan was not shown better than the rules', so the rules serve. Both plans enforce only about a third of the planted traps.
lessons: Two reviews before a one-time run found 23 issues; 3 of them alone would have decided the result.
A wrapper that catches every exception can turn an arm into its baseline without a trace: record every failed request.
Count only what was measured: a default of 0 seconds is not a time.
risks: The held-out set is used; any fix tuned on its counts is not proven.
Small sample: the interval of check 5 is wide.
